newsitem.title: UK: First Cuba order emerges on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: First Cuba order emerges on sugar freight market.

text.p: Brazilian demand remained uppermost on the sugar freight market on Thursday, accompanied by the first order seen to ship sugar from Cuba's 1996/97 cane crop, shipbrokers said.
Although the order was not confirmed, market sources cited talk that Nissho Iwai was open for 24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Japan for early January shipment dates.
Elsewhere, Louis Dreyfus was said to have fixed 14,250 tonnes of bagged sugar from Recife to the Red Sea for mid-November. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.

Brazilian shippers SIMAB were also active on Thursday, fixing their earlier order for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Recife to Lagos for around November 5/15 and quoting for 12,000 tonnes, again in bags, from Paranagua to the Red Sea for mid-November.
Genoc quoted two new prompt orders for bagged sugar with similar destinations, shipbrokers said.
It was open for 13/14,000 tonnes from Poland to the Mediterranean/Red Sea and the same tonnage from Santos to the Mediterranean with Black Sea, Red Sea and Indian Ocean options.
Booker for 10,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Georgetown to Kantvik for mid-November and Seven Seas was in the market for 14,000 tonnes in bags from north Brazil to the Mediterranean for similar dates.
